  "raw_idea": "The reliability of open‑domain question answering drops sharply when source texts are continuously amended, as in statutes, policies, or regulations. In such settings each new amendment supersedes earlier clauses while retaining much of the original wording, creating a dense semantic overlap across successive versions. We propose to develop a retrieval‑agnostic framework that enriches any standard document retriever with a temporal relevance component: the rank of a candidate passage will be adjusted according to the elapsed time between the query’s target date and the passage’s version timestamp, while still leveraging its semantic similarity to the query. If confirmed by full-text reading, the idea's mechanism and benchmark contribution are largely pre-empted; the remaining delta would be domain (statutes/regulations) and the retrieval-agnostic framing.
input.rationale: Titles and the available abstract of the 'Bridging the Temporal-Semantic Gap' paper explicitly describe combining lexical, dense, and exponential temporal decay signals and building a temporal benchmark -- the core of the proposed method.

input.question: Does adjusting rank by elapsed time between the query target date and the passage version timestamp (a recency-like signal) actually identify the legally correct passage, or is the correct signal validity/as-of membership (the version in force at the target date), which recency can get wrong?
input.description: For statutes/regulations the authoritative clause is the one in force at the query's target date. A superseded version may be temporally closer (more 'recent-looking') than an older version still in force, and a not-yet-in-force version may be nearest of all. If the framework conflates recency with validity, the temporal term could systematically select wrong revisions. Retrieved point-in-time work instead enforces an as-of information boundary.
input.rationale: TempFinRAG enforces an as-of temporal boundary defined by filing availability rather than mere recency, indicating the field distinguishes validity from closeness in time.

input.question: Is a versioned regulatory corpus with reliable validity intervals (in-force start/end dates) and time-stamped queries actually available or constructible at reasonable cost?
input.description: The framework and its benchmark require per-passage validity metadata and queries with target dates. Existing temporal benchmarks cover ESG disclosures and SEC filings; availability of equivalent amendment/validity metadata for statutes or regulations is unverified.
input.rationale: Retrieved temporal benchmarks are in ESG and financial domains; no retrieved work confirms an equivalent amended-statute benchmark with validity intervals.
